newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine banks open for strike, but business thin.
newsitem.headline: Argentine banks open for strike, but business thin.

text.p: Argentina's Central Bank said a 36-hour general strike which began at noon/1100 EDT Thursday was not affecting banking operations, but private bankers said business and market activity was thin.

"Banking activities are being carried out normally in the whole country," said a Central Bank spokesman, adding that only branches in Buenos Aires' central Plaza de Mayo, where a union rally was scheduled to take place, had closed.

But the Banking Association union, calling on members to strike against the Peronist government's drive for fiscal austerity and more flexible labor laws, said many banks had stopped attending the public when the strike began.

One local banker told Reuters that union members had been driving around the city's financial center "calling on workers to join in the strike," and had thrown "stink bombs" in two banks to scare away customers.

"We believe activity will be normal, though some branches are going to work with the shutters down to avoid trouble with strikers," he said. Some banks were considering closing shop mid-afternoon to avoid workers' having problems getting home due to planned transport stoppages, he said.
In the local financial markets, dealers said trading was thin and most business was done before noon.
"It is a wasted day. In the morning, prices were normal but there wasn't anyone ready to do business," said one foreign exchange dealer.
